answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing as-is cannot meet the primary objective. Memory c2 documents that switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Before I commit, I want to verify c2 against the archived source: I need to confirm the prior switch was on a comparable component, that the volume/onboarding profile maps to our 94%-utilization line, and that no hidden risk (lead time, quality, contractual penalty) was lost in consolidation. With 14 days to expiry and no auto-renew, timing supports a guarded primary switch. To cap delivery risk to the 94%-utilized line with no buffer, I would stage this as a limited parallel / ramped transition rather than an abrupt flip, starting on a subset of volume and expanding only if cost and on-time delivery track. A second source addition (memory c3) would hedge risk further but is not feasible inside one decision this cycle and does not by itself deliver the mandated 18% cut. Verdict: switch primary vendor to the low-cost supplier, in a small guarded test, with the option to scale once verified.
